title: Play the Census 2021 population map game
meta_description: Higher or lower game made with Census 2021 data. Guess if the next local authority area has more or fewer residents than the previous one.

breadcrumb.text: Play the Census 2021 population map game

lede: Move across England and Wales by correctly guessing if the number of people living in an area is higher or lower than others.

body.text: Can you guess whether the next local authority area you land on has more or fewer residents than the previous one, according to Census 2021? Complete your trip in as few guesses as possible.
You can share your score on social media and challenge your friends. You can come back to this page to play our daily game, with a new route each day, or try our other game modes.

body.text: The first results from Census 2021 provide [early rounded population estimates for England and Wales](https://www.ons.gov.uk/peoplepopulationandcommunity/populationandmigration/populationestimates/bulletins/populationandhouseholdestimatesenglandandwales/census2021). Unrounded figures will be released in autumn 2022. Figures may differ slightly in future releases because of the impact of removing rounding and applying further statistical processes.

Area in square kilometres, excluding inland water, is taken from the 2021 [standard area measurements for local authority areas](https://geoportal.statistics.gov.uk/datasets/ons::standard-area-measurements-latest-for-administrative-areas-in-the-united-kingdom-v2/about).
Population density is the estimated number of usual residents per square kilometre. It has been calculated using population estimates rounded to the nearest hundred.
